[debt-collectors-collections] Scope: debt buyers, third-party collection agencies and high-volume collection law firms that send collection letters to U.S. consumers (bill_type 'other'). Completeness was checked against the CFPB Consumer Complaint Database: all 'Debt collection' complaints received 2023-01-01 through 2026-09-30 (743,780 complaints; 3,787 companies). After removing credit bureaus, card issuers, banks, lenders, BNPL and loan/student-loan servicers (they are covered in other categories), every collector in the CFPB top ~375 ranks is in this file or in an existing category file. Detailed tier (about 60 firms): the collectors behind roughly the top 35 CFPB collector names, including Resurgent/LVNV, Jefferson Capital (CFPB: CL Holdings), Midland/Encore, PRA, Credit Collection Services (CFPB: CCS Financial Services), Credence (CFPB: Kriya Capital), National Credit Systems, Caine & Weiner, Spring Oaks, Columbia Debt Recovery/Genesis, National Credit Adjusters, Radius, Hunter Warfield, Sunrise, Aldous, TrueAccord, Harris & Harris, NCB, FCO, ProCollect, Credit Control, Sequium, SourceRM, AmSher/InDebted, NRA Group, Security Credit Services, CPC, Cavalry, plus Phillips & Cohen (estates), Weltman and Linebarger. Each has its payment portal, payment-plan route, dispute/validation route where published, phones and mailing address, and each links to CFPB/FTC scam checks. Roster tier: the next 150 collector names from the CFPB ranking (ranks 22-375, not already covered). 64 of them have an official website confirmed by fetching it this session. The rest have website=null because the web-search budget ran out mid-run and guessed domains could not be confirmed. Deliberately not repeated here: IC System, TSI, CBE, AR Resources, CMRE, State Collection Service, Americollect, Medicredit, HRRG, Grant & Weber, Firstsource, Frost-Arnett, Medical Data Systems and Penn Credit are in medical-billing.json. Monterey Financial is in personal-student-bnpl.json. Radius, Credence and Harris & Harris were named in the task, so they are kept here with collections-side detail and cross-referenced. Alias rows (tier roster) point Account Control Technology and Convergent Outsourcing to TSI. Status rows: Performant has exited consumer collections, Diversified Consultants closed in 2020, and Receivables Performance Management has closed. Still missing: (1) official consumer sites for ERC/Enhanced Recovery (ercbpo.com failed the TLS handshake) and Stoneleigh (its old domain now goes to a spam site). Their entries use unverified third-party data and are marked verified=false. (2) Websites for about 86 roster rows, including the high-volume names Southwest Credit Systems, United Collection Bureau, Eastern Account System, Diversified Adjustment, RentDebt, Waypoint, Williams & Fudge and Northstar. (3) The brand behind CFPB holding names T.S. Holdings, V and H Portfolio, Collection Management Holdings, BTH Management and CLGF Holdco. (4) Small local and regional collectors below about 140 complaints, and collection law firms outside the top ranks. For those, a senior should use the name and phone on their letter plus NMLS Consumer Access or their state's collection-agency licensing lookup. Several phone labels (pay-by-phone vs. general) and remit P.O. boxes come from the collector's site, but some remit boxes come only from third-party sources, and notes flag these. REVIEWER PASS (2026-09-30): Now 217 entries, 66 detailed and 127 marked verified. (1) URL re-check: every URL in the file was requested again by HTTP. About 35 detailed entries were also re-read in a real browser, because several sites time out or block plain HTTP clients but load normally; these include Midland, NCB, NRA and UCB. (2) Fixes: LMM's payment link was dead (it redirected to the homepage) and now points to lmm1.cssimpact.com. The AmSher Virtual Collector link now goes to InDebted's portal at payment.indebted.us. The Credence Pay page uses an APS gateway, and payment plans there are set up by phone only. NRA's consumer site, nationalrecovery.com, was found; it has a portal for balance, history, payments and payment plans, plus its remit P.O. box. ONLINE Information Services now has its consumer portal (a DAKCS-hosted app) and collections phone (800) 286-2487. Client Services uses PaymentVision, and a balance/history request goes through its FAQ and contact route. USCB now has its dispute and paid-in-full pages and office address. Weltman lists different toll-free numbers on weltman.com and on its wwrepay portal; both are recorded. Linebarger's LGBS Web Payments portal covers court fees, fines and tolls. NCB's consumer and business phone numbers are now told apart. (3) Mergers: Frontline Asset Strategies accounts are now serviced by Radius Global Solutions, and both entries note this. Wakefield is cross-referenced to medical-billing.json, and the roster row 'Central Research' to CRI in personal-student-bnpl.json. (4) Upgrades from roster to detailed: United Collection Bureau, Contract Callers, Zwicker & Associates, Reliant Capital Solutions and Southwest Recovery Services. Websites were added for Synerprise, Frontline (now Radius) and Lloyd & McDaniel. (5) For 35 detailed entries that had a plan/recurring-payment route but no cancel page, autopay_cancel now points to the collector's contact/help page. The notes say so, because collectors do not publish self-service cancel pages. Still open: ERC's site (ercbpo.com) still fails TLS in both HTTP and browser checks. Stoneleigh has no official site. The brands behind the CFPB names T.S. Holdings, V and H Portfolio, Collection Management Holdings, BTH Management and CLGF Holdco 1 are still unknown: the public CFPB API returns no complaint narratives, and web search was unavailable in this pass. rentdebt.com and diversifiedadjustment.com resolve but sit behind interactive captchas, so they were not confirmed or recorded as websites. The roster-row websites for Southwest Credit Systems, Eastern Account System, Credit Corp Solutions, Waypoint and Williams & Fudge are still unconfirmed; the guessed domains were parked or for sale. The Credit Control and Caine & Weiner portals remain behind Cloudflare. REVIEWER PASS 2 (2026-09-30, web search available): Now 217 entries, 75 detailed, 139 verified. (1) ERC is resolved: its consumer help now lives on ercglobalcx.com (payment FAQ, dispute FAQ, payment and correspondence P.O. boxes, (800) 383-5979). The entry is now verified. The self-service portal host it names (ssp.ercbpo.com) still did not answer plain HTTP. (2) Nine high-volume roster rows were upgraded to detailed from their official sites: Southwest Credit Systems (swcconsumer.com, EvokePay), Credit Corp Solutions (creditcorponline.com), Waypoint Resource Group, RentDebt Automated Collections, Diversified Adjustment Service (both loaded normally this time), Debt Recovery Solutions (DAKCS portal), The Receivable Management Services (Virtual Collector portal), Williams & Fudge (PayWFC; Paymentus/PayRazr links) and Synergetic Communication. (3) Afni now has its consumer portal (afnicollections.com / payments.afnicollections.com) with plan and dispute routes. (4) Status and identity: hlv.com (Helvey & Associates) now redirects to cacionline.net (CACi / Consumer Adjustment Company), and both rows note this. The domain listed for Stoneleigh now goes to a gambling spam site, and the entry warns not to use it. CLGF Holdco 1 is a debt-buying vehicle acquired by Castlelake (FTC early-termination notice 20250987). United Revenue's own contact page and phones were confirmed. (5) Recorded as unverified because the sites blocked automated fetches: Eastern Account System (easternaccounts.com, Cloudflare 403), First Credit Services (firstcreditonline.com, 403) and CACi (cacionline.net, timeout). Their websites came from search results. (6) Re-check: every URL on the detailed entries (289) was requested again. 285 returned HTTP 200. The 4 that did not are ssp.ercbpo.com, plus the Credit Control and Caine & Weiner (connectcw.com) pages, which are behind Cloudflare. Still open: the brands behind T.S. Holdings, V and H Portfolio, Collection Management Holdings and BTH Management (BTH Inc., Santa Barbara, per search) are unknown. Optio and FirstPoint still publish no consumer payment portal. Roster rows below roughly 450 complaints mostly still have website=null.

[debt-relief-credit-counseling] Checked against: (a) the NFCC member-agency lists on nfcc.org (/nfcc-member-agencies/ and the /current-members/ agency dropdown, ~55 names incl. 3 Canadian agencies that were excluded); (b) the U.S. Trustee Program list of approved credit counseling agencies, scraped from all per-state pages on justice.gov (65 unique agencies; AL and NC are Bankruptcy Administrator districts and have no UST page; the paginated national list blocked '?page=' requests, but state pages cover all national agencies). Pure bankruptcy-course vendors (Simple Class, BK Class, 1$ Wiser, BKCert, DollarBK, Evergreen, FES Courses, DebtorCC, 123 Credit Counselors, Access Counseling, The Kingdom Ministries) were excluded because they do not run monthly plans. Detailed tier: the major national nonprofits named in scope (MMI incl. ClearPoint/CCCS Atlanta/CCCS Maryland legacy, GreenPath, Cambridge incl. Pioneer, InCharge, ACCC, Consolidated Credit, Apprisen, Navicore incl. Novadebt, Take Charge America, Debt Reduction Services/Money Fit, Credit.org/Springboard) plus regional agencies with public client portals; the major debt settlement companies (National Debt Relief, Freedom Debt Relief, Accredited, Beyond Finance, Americor, ClearOne Advantage, Pacific Debt, JG Wentworth, Achieve, CuraDebt, DMB, Liberty, Alleviate, United Settlement); processors Global Holdings and CFTPay; tax firms Optima, Tax Defense Network, Community Tax, Anthem, Clear Start, Alleviate Tax. Several sites (Apprisen, Take Charge America, JG Wentworth, Community Tax, Origin SC, CFTPay) are behind bot checks and were read with a real browser session (no logins, no forms). Observations: many agencies use Client Support Software hosted portals (extranet*.clientsupportsoftware.com) - InCharge, Take Charge America, DebtWave, CCCS Rochester, Consumer Debt Counselors, FamilyMeans. Settlement companies rarely publish deposit-change/cancel pages; their FAQs say clients own the dedicated account and may withdraw anytime. Gaps: FCAA does not publish a member list (zip-code finder only), so FCAA-only members beyond those in the UST/NFCC lists may be missing; websites for several small NFCC members (CCCS of Hampton Roads, Huntington, Greater Milwaukee, Mobile, Family & Community Services, Financial Pathways of the Piedmont, Tabor, Parkview, Family Foundations) could not be confirmed (web search unavailable this session); Reliant Account Management, EPPS and Crossroads Financial Technologies have no confirmable public site, and Meracord shows 'Coming Soon'; Freedom Debt Relief's current-client phone renders as a template placeholder on its contact page; payment remit P.O. boxes are mostly unpublished (use the address on your statement); debt-settlement roster is not exhaustive (hundreds of small firms and law-firm models exist; ACDR/AADR member lists were not retrieved). Added FORTH Pay (Set Forth, LLC) as a detailed dedicated-account processor (client.forthpay.com, 877-800-5577) - a major processor missing from the original pass. Added Turnbull Law Group, Tax Network USA, Fortress Tax Relief (roster). Re-checked the US Trustee CSV: remaining unmatched rows are bankruptcy-course-only vendors (Simple Class, Debtorcc, 1$ Wiser, BK Cert, Dollar Learning, Evergreen, FES, Kingdom Ministries, BK Class, 123 Credit Counselors, Access Counseling) or alternate domains of agencies already present (ACCC, InCharge, credit.org). NFCC list re-read: Money Mentors, Credit Canada and Credit Counselling Society are Canadian (out of scope; moneymentors.org is a parked domain). (2) Accuracy - HTTP-checked every URL in the file (~210); all official pages resolve except bot-protected sites (Apprisen, Take Charge America, JG Wentworth, Community Tax, Origin SC, TaxRise, Larson, New Era - previously browser-verified) and a few dead roster domains (cccsoftheozarks.org, sixcscreditcounseling.com). Phone numbers on detailed entries were matched against their own pages. Fixes: Freedom Debt Relief current-client phone now 800-655-6303 (contact page); LSS MN portal now redirects to Cloverleaf CMS; Alleviate website set to alleviate.com; credit.org statement/progress-report guidance; Rescue One phone clarified; Consumer Credit Counseling Foundation upgraded to detailed; duplicate Money Fit by DRS roster entry merged into Debt Reduction Services. Web search budget was exhausted during review, so new firms were found from rosters and direct site reads only. GAP-FILL PASS 2026-10-02 (web search available): resolved previously unconfirmed NFCC members - CCCS of Mobile (Lifelines Counseling Services), CCCS of Huntington (Goodwill KYOWVA; FinCo CMS client site), CCCS of Greater Milwaukee (Aurora Family Service), Financial Pathways of the Piedmont (upgraded to detailed; DMPs serviced by Navicore), Tabor Community Services merged into Tenfold (wearetenfold.org; duplicate 'Tenfold' entry removed), CCCS of Family & Community Services merged into Axess Family Services (no DMP shown), Family Foundations = Family Foundations of Northeast Florida (Jacksonville; bot-blocked, unverified), CCCS of Hampton Roads = Center for Child & Family Services (DMP status unclear; old debtfreeonline.com domain now an unrelated lender). Reliant Account Management confirmed at reliantpayment.com (consumer support 877-859-1450). Still unresolved: EPPS (no official consumer site found), Meracord (site 'Coming Soon'), Crossroads Financial Technologies, Parkview Services (bot-blocked; location unconfirmed). Added Instant Tax Solutions. REVIEWER PASS 2026-10-02: (1) HTTP-checked every URL in detailed entries (172 URLs) and re-read 26 detailed entries' pages via fetch. Fixed: Anthem Tax installment-agreement link (old path 404 -> /tax-relief-services/...); Navicore portal link on its own site (/Account/LogOn) now 404s, kept working /login; Optima portal now redirects to plans.optimatax.com; Freedom Debt Relief autopay_cancel now points to FAQ (3-business-day notice to stop next deposit); filled autopay_cancel/help links for DebtWave, Credit Advisors, Consumer Debt Counselors; existing-client phone lines added/corrected for Family Credit (877-322-8330), ClearOne Client Relations (888-744-9361), Pacific Debt hours, DebtWave hours; DMCC noted as partnered with Take Charge America; MMI notes record that cccsmd.org, cccsatl.org and clearpointccs.org redirect to moneymanagement.org; CuraDebt client logon did not respond. Summit Financial Education confirmed as bankruptcy-course-only (no DMP). (2) Completeness: all 32 ACDR member firms are present. The 14 U.S. Trustee-approved agencies not in this file were checked; those read (Debtorcc, 123 Credit Counselors -> bankruptcyclass.com, Summit) offer only bankruptcy counseling/education courses with no monthly plan, and the rest are bankruptcy-course brands by name (Simple Class, 1$ Wiser, Bk Class, Dollar Learning, Evergreen Class, bkcert, FES Courses) or duplicates of ACCC/InCharge/credit.org domains, so they were not added. Added CCCS of Central Oklahoma (detailed, NFCC), Oak View Law Group (roster; not accepting new clients) and Heartland Tax Solutions (roster). Web search budget was exhausted in this pass, so candidates were found by direct domain checks only; BALANCE (balancepro.org) shows no DMP on its homepage and was not added.

entries.phone_customer_service: 501-682-1001 (DHS main line; no unit line published)

entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: REVIEW 2026-10-02: still no estate recovery web page on humanservices.arkansas.gov (site search returned none). The official Arkansas Medical Services Policy Manual is published as Code of Arkansas Rules 20 CAR pt. 500 (webftp.blr.arkansas.gov PDF, version 9.1.2026, fetched). Section H-600 covers recovery from people 55+ who got nursing-facility, ICF/IID or HCBS waiver care, and from people of any age who were permanently institutionalized. There is no recovery while a spouse, a child under 21 or a blind/disabled child survives, when recovery would cause undue hardship, or when it is not cost-effective. Beneficiary-deed interests are exempt (Act 570 of 2021). Section H-730 (6/1/2025): the personal representative or distributee may request a hardship waiver within 35 days of the DHS notice by mailing a statement with supporting documents to the TPL Unit address. Factors include a sole income-producing asset, the heir becoming benefit-eligible, a home valued at 50% or less of the county average, and other compelling circumstances. Payment instructions come with the DHS notice of intent to recover. The same PDF is linked as view_bill and payment_assistance.

Social Security/SSI/VA benefits are generally protected from garnishment by private collectors (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/can-a-debt-collector-take-my-social-security-or-va-benefits-en-1157/ ). entries.name: Family Credit Management
entries.parent_company: Family Credit Counseling Service, Inc. d/b/a Family Credit Management (nonprofit)
entries.service_area_detail: Rockford, IL; nationwide by phone. NFCC member; UST-approved.
entries.senior_programs: Offers 'Priority Repayment Plan' and 'DualTrack' hybrid repayment options in addition to standard DMPs.
entries.notes: Client Login is a Salesforce Experience site (familycreditmanagement.my.site.com). Phone for deposit changes/cancellation. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/ . Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent. Reviewer 2026-10-02: homepage lists a dedicated existing-client line 877-322-8330. FAQ (https://www.familycredit.org/faq): monthly statement shows where the money went, online account shows status anytime; 2025 averages were $28/month fee and $39 one-time enrollment fee, both included in the monthly payment.

entries.notes: Consumer Bill of Rights page https://www.aargon.com/bill-of-rights.html ; FAQ covers authorizing a third party (e.g., family member) to discuss the account. Mailing address is on your notice. autopay_cancel points to the collector's contact/help page: no self-service 'cancel plan' page is published, so stop or change a payment plan or recurring payment by calling the listed number or writing to the collector (and tell your bank to stop any ACH debit you revoked). Scam check: never pay a caller you cannot verify - look up the collector's number yourself (not from the call/text), ask for the written validation notice, and compare with CFPB 'debt collector or scammer?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-can-i-tell-if-a-caller-is-a-debt-collector-or-a-scammer-en-1699/ and FTC 'Fake and abusive debt collectors' https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/fake-abusive-debt-collectors . Dispute/validation: under the FDCPA/Reg F you can dispute in writing within the 30-day validation period and the collector must pause collection until it sends verification (CFPB rights: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/debt-collection/answers/know-your-rights/ ). Social Security/SSI/VA benefits are generally protected from garnishment by private collectors (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/can-a-debt-collector-take-my-social-security-or-va-benefits-en-1157/ ). Complaints: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ .

entries.parent_company: Beyond Finance, LLC (Accredited Debt Relief is a Beyond Finance brand; private, for-profit)
entries.service_area_detail: Debt settlement/consolidation marketer; mailing P.O. Box 660442, Dallas, TX 75266-0442; not available in all states. Fees 15%-25% of enrolled debt.
entries.phone_customer_service: 1-800-497-1965 (client Support Team; Mon-Fri 8am-11pm, Sat-Sun 8am-10pm ET); corporate 800-282-7186
entries.mail_payment_address: Accredited Debt Relief, P.O. Box 660442, Dallas, TX 75266-0442 (general mailing address)
entries.payment_processor: independent third-party dedicated-account provider ($9.00 set-up + $9.75/month per FAQ; provider not named)
entries.senior_programs: Has a 'Seniors on Fixed Incomes' page in site navigation; no fee waivers.
entries.notes: Clients monitor progress via a personal client dashboard / mobile app with direct messaging (customer-service page); no public web login URL found. FAQ: 'every client program requires a dedicated account owned and controlled by the client and operated by an independent third-party provider'. Company says it never asks for payment upfront and won't message via Facebook - beware impostors. Change deposit/cancel by calling 800-497-1965. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ , FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ , and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general . ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint . Reviewer 2026-10-02: customer-service page re-read: clients reach support by phone 800-497-1965, mobile-app messaging or email 365 days a year; app gives 24/7 progress visibility.

entries.name: Achieve Debt Relief (Achieve Resolution)
entries.parent_company: Achieve (formerly Freedom Financial Network; sister brand of Freedom Debt Relief)
entries.service_area_detail: Debt resolution program marketed under the Achieve brand; Tempe, AZ / San Mateo, CA.
entries.payment_processor: dedicated account provider per program agreement (Achieve affiliate Crossroads Financial Technologies is used by Freedom Debt Relief)
entries.notes: Achieve sign-in covers its products; Achieve GOOD app also offered. Debt relief program details/cancellation via Achieve contact center. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ , FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ , and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general . ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint . Reviewer 2026-10-02: contact page re-read shows only 1-800-920-0045 and a contact form; no Achieve Resolution-specific client line on that page.

entries.senior_programs: DMP fees: one-time $50 set-up and $10-$50/month based on number of creditors; may be reduced or waived depending on state law.
entries.notes: Client Login page: DMP clients can 'access all of your account information, manage and review your accounts online, check when your next payment is due'. Draft changes/cancellation by phone 866-699-2227. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/ . Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent.

entries.name: Afni
entries.service_area_detail: Large collector/BPO (Bloomington, IL) for telecom/wireless, insurance subrogation and utility clients. CFPB complaints since 2023: 413.
entries.mail_payment_address: Afni, Inc., P.O. Box 3517, Bloomington, IL 61702.
entries.notes: Reviewer 2026-09-30 (pass 2): Afni's consumer collections site is afnicollections.com (separate from the corporate afni.com). Its secure portal lets you review the account, pay in full or set up a future payment schedule, and dispute via the 'unable to make a payment' link (FAQ: https://afnicollections.com/faqs). Same phone 866-352-0479 and P.O. Box 3517, Bloomington, IL 61702. No self-service cancel page - call or use Contact Us to stop a scheduled payment. Afni often collects final wireless/cable bills (e.g., carriers' unreturned-equipment charges) - ask for itemization. Scam check: never pay a caller you cannot verify - look up the collector's number yourself (not from the call/text), ask for the written validation notice, and compare with CFPB 'debt collector or scammer?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-can-i-tell-if-a-caller-is-a-debt-collector-or-a-scammer-en-1699/ and FTC 'Fake and abusive debt collectors' https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/fake-abusive-debt-collectors . Dispute/validation: under the FDCPA/Reg F you can dispute in writing within the 30-day validation period and the collector must pause collection until it sends verification (CFPB rights: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/debt-collection/answers/know-your-rights/ ). Social Security/SSI/VA benefits are generally protected from garnishment by private collectors (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/can-a-debt-collector-take-my-social-security-or-va-benefits-en-1157/ ). Complaints: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ .

entries.notes: Existing clients: 'Log into your Client Dashboard' (activation at beyondfinance.com/registration/new) or the Beyond Finance app. Contact page lists separate email boxes for Client Success, general documents, legal documents and complaints. FAQ: single monthly deposit into a Dedicated Account 'that you control... You own the account and the money in it'; fees only after an offer you approve and payments begin. To change the deposit or cancel, contact Client Success by phone or chat. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ , FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ , and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general . ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint . entries.service_area_detail: Debt settlement company; not available in all states.
entries.notes: Roster only. Site blocks automated readers (HTTP 202 challenge); not reviewed. ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint . Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . entries.notes: Roster only. Client login uses debtfreeportal.com. ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint . Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ , FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ , and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general .

Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Contact page has an online inquiry form. Scam check: never pay a caller you cannot verify - look up the collector's number yourself (not from the call/text), ask for the written validation notice, and compare with CFPB 'debt collector or scammer?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-can-i-tell-if-a-caller-is-a-debt-collector-or-a-scammer-en-1699/ and FTC 'Fake and abusive debt collectors' https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/fake-abusive-debt-collectors . Complaints: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ .

entries.service_area_detail: Consumer-facing aggregator claiming 120,000+ payable billers; public directory at https://www.doxo.com/u/bills-to-pay (browse by service and location)
entries.mail_payment_address: doxo, PO Box 1202, Bellevue, WA 98009 (correspondence; not a biller remittance address)
entries.payment_processor: doxo; payments processed by Cass Commercial Bank (Member FDIC) with Truex Payments, Inc. delivering instructions
entries.notes: CAUTION FOR SENIORS: The FTC sued Doxo and its co-founders (complaint filed April 25, 2024) alleging misleading search ads that impersonated consumers' billers and undisclosed fees; FTC case page (https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings/doxo) reports a $2.1 million settlement (dated Aug 17, 2026). doxo is NOT the biller; its own help says if a payment is overdue or must arrive quickly, pay the biller directly. Autopay (auto schedule) is fixed-amount only, drafts about 15 days before due date, and requires one prior manual payment; cancel instructions not on that page (same page reused). Fees (https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-payment-fees-are-calculated-and-activating-free-payments/): ACH $2.99 or $3.99 may apply, cards typically 3-3.5% of the amount; free when paying from a linked bank account in the doxo Wallet; doxoPLUS $5.99/month (cancel: https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-can-i-cancel-my-doxoplus-subscription/). Scheduled payments can be edited/cancelled only before processing starts; after that ask the biller for a credit/refund. Support 1-855-791-9986, chat, Mon-Fri 5am-5pm PT (https://www.doxo.com/w/about/contact/). The app should prefer biller-direct links over doxo. Some billers (e.g., National Grid) list doxo as a paperless/delivery option. Other useful doxo help: cancel doxoPLUS https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-can-i-cancel-my-doxoplus-subscription/ ; close doxo account https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-do-i-cancel-my-doxo-account/ ; disconnect a provider https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-do-i-disconnect-from-a-provider/ ; contact https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-can-i-contact-doxo-customer-service/ ; doxo biller directory FAQ https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/what-billers-can-i-pay-through-doxos-bill-pay-platform/ ; doxo's response to FTC https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/are-the-ftc-allegations-against-doxo-true/. entries.name: EPPS (Electronic Payment Provider Services) - debt settlement dedicated accounts
entries.notes: Dedicated-account/payment processor used by some debt settlement and student-loan document-prep companies. No official website confirmed (eppsinc.com shows a 'Launching Soon' placeholder; epps.com is an unrelated consulting firm). Contact your debt relief company for the EPPS account statement and to stop drafts. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ , FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ , and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general . Web searches on 2026-10-02 also found no official EPPS consumer site; 'EPP' is also used generically for any electronic payment provider holding a dedicated account.

entries.service_area_detail: Solar lease/PPA/loan provider; EIA-861 rows IL/OH ~3,500, TX ~2,300, MD/NJ, CO
entries.notes: Contact page (fetched 2026-09-30): once the system is in service customers get an email invitation to register for MyEverBright to view balance, make a payment, see agreement details and chat with Homeowner Support. Autopay not described publicly. Rooftop solar lease/PPA/loan bill is separate from the utility bill - the senior still gets a (smaller) utility bill for delivery charges and any power used beyond the panels. Missing solar payments does not cut off electricity but can lead to collections and, for loans, a UCC-1 fixture filing on the equipment (not a mortgage lien). There is no 'switch back to the utility' for a lease/PPA: the contract runs 20-25 years; options are buyout/prepayment, transfer to a home buyer, or early termination per contract. entries.name: FORTH Pay (Set Forth, LLC) - debt settlement dedicated accounts

entries.notes: Consumer Help Hub FAQ: view account details and statements at client.forthpay.com or by calling 877-800-5577; to change payment date or amount, contact your debt relief service provider (DRSP) first because changes can affect pending settlements; banking-information updates go through your DRSP or FORTH (877-800-5577, clients@setforth.com). FORTH does not process ACH on bank holidays (schedule on the help hub). Setup/cancel links point to the same help-hub FAQ. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . entries.notes: Client Portal page: DMP clients 'log in now to check your account balances and monitor the progress of your Debt Management Program' and chat with staff; separate Bankruptcy Portal for certificates. Deposit changes/stopping drafts/cancelling: call Client Services 866-476-7284 (contact page: 'DMP clients can log in to My Portal or call us directly to reach a Client Success Specialist'). FAQ: the DMP agreement 'is not a binding contract and you can cancel the program at any time'; removing a debt usually returns it to original APR. Same portal URL reused for view/pay/history. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/ . Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent. Reviewer 2026-10-02: contact page links My Portal at myportal.greenpath.com/Account_UI/Login.aspx; DMP clients log in or call Client Success 866-476-7284; general counseling 844-939-2481; HQ 36500 Corporate Dr., Farmington Hills, MI 48331.

entries.name: GRT Financial
entries.service_area_detail: Debt settlement company; not available in all states.
entries.notes: Roster only. Michigan-based debt resolution company. ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint . Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ , FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ , and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general .

entries.service_area_detail: Debt buyer/collector (Sartell, MN) buying charged-off credit card, telecom, auto and other accounts. CFPB lists it as 'CL Holdings LLC': 39,058 debt collection complaints since 2023.
entries.mail_payment_address: Correspondence: Jefferson Capital Systems, LLC, 200 14th Ave E, Sartell, MN 56377. Use the remit P.O. box printed on your letter for payments (third-party sources cite P.O. Box 772813, Chicago, IL 60677-2813 - unverified).
entries.payment_processor: in-house (myjcap.com portal); rewards emails from yourjcapaccount.com / yourpaymentrewards.com (PaymentRewards program)
entries.notes: jcap.com 'Contact our Consumer Account Support Department' links to myjcap.com consumer portal (Payment Options, FAQ, Login). FAQ confirms emails from yourjcapaccount.com and yourpaymentrewards.com are legitimate. Payment Options page is script-rendered and did not load; dispute address not published (write to Sartell address). Reviewer 2026-09-30: jcap.com homepage re-checked (phone 833-851-5552; FAQ and Contact Us links; also links PaymentRewards.com, a JCap payment-rewards program). autopay_cancel points to the collector's contact/help page: no self-service 'cancel plan' page is published, so stop or change a payment plan or recurring payment by calling the listed number or writing to the collector (and tell your bank to stop any ACH debit you revoked). Scam check: never pay a caller you cannot verify - look up the collector's number yourself (not from the call/text), ask for the written validation notice, and compare with CFPB 'debt collector or scammer?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-can-i-tell-if-a-caller-is-a-debt-collector-or-a-scammer-en-1699/ and FTC 'Fake and abusive debt collectors' https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/fake-abusive-debt-collectors . Dispute/validation: under the FDCPA/Reg F you can dispute in writing within the 30-day validation period and the collector must pause collection until it sends verification (CFPB rights: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/debt-collection/answers/know-your-rights/ ). Social Security/SSI/VA benefits are generally protected from garnishment by private collectors (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/can-a-debt-collector-take-my-social-security-or-va-benefits-en-1157/ ). Complaints: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ .

entries.payment_processor: third-party dedicated account provider (not named on public pages)
entries.notes: Site is behind a bot challenge (read via real browser). Login page has separate 'Debt Relief Customers' portal (my.jgwentworth.com) vs 'Loan Customers' (debt resolution loans, loans.jgwentworth.com) - check enrollment paperwork for which product you have. Deposit changes/cancellation: call 888-570-5240 or email debt@jgwentworth.com. JG Wentworth also buys structured settlements/annuities - a different product. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ , FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ , and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general . ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint .

entries.name: KUBRA (EZ-PAY / EZ-PAY+)
entries.service_area_detail: Bill presentment (iDoxs), payments (EZ-PAY), outage maps and notifications for large utilities, government and insurers in US/Canada
entries.notes: EZ-PAY answers page: KUBRA does not take payments on its own site; pay via your service provider's EZ-PAY link; guest one-time payment needs only account number; payments show almost instantly with a confirmation number; for problems contact the service provider. Support page (https://www.kubra.com/support) says contact your biller first, then KUBRA Consumer Support portal https://consumersupport.kubra.com/csp (JS-rendered). EZ-PAY+ product page (https://www.kubra.com/products-and-services/billing-and-payments/kubra-ez-pay) says payers can schedule, cancel and review payment history in the biller-branded wallet; supports card, ACH, PIN-less debit, Apple/Google Pay, cash at retail, natural-language IVR. No public consumer phone found; no public biller directory. Platform does not hold the consumer's account; the biller owns bill view, autopay and history. Direct the senior to the biller's own portal (see the biller's entry in the other category files). CLIENTS (from repo cross-reference): KUBRA: 70 billers in this repo's category files use it (rosters/payment_platform_usage_xref.csv); largest: Xcel Energy - Colorado (Public Service Company of Colorado) (CO); Xcel Energy (Northern States Power Co - Minnesota) (MN|ND|SD); Eversource (Massachusetts) - NSTAR Electric (incl. former Western Massachusetts Electric) (MA); Xcel Energy - Colorado (Public Service Company of Colorado) (CO); Eversource (Connecticut) - formerly Connecticut Light & Power (CL&P) (CT); Washington Gas (DC|MD|VA); CPS Energy (TX); Tampa Electric (TECO) (FL); Xcel Energy (Northern States Power) – gas (MN|ND|WI|MI); PNM (Public Service Company of New Mexico) (NM) REVIEW 2026-09-29: EZ-PAY answers page re-fetched: KUBRA says it reaches over 40% of US and Canadian households; one-time payments need only the account number; biller sees the payment almost instantly, sometimes next business day; for problems, contact your service provider first, then the KUBRA Support Portal. Autopay setup and cancel, and payment history, are handled in the biller-branded wallet or portal (KUBRA MyHQ+/EZ-PAY+), not on kubra.com, so those links stay null. No consumer phone is published. REVIEW2 2026-09-29: Re-fetched ez-pay-answers: KUBRA does not take payments on its own site; pay through the service provider's site; OTP = guest one-time payment the provider authorized; payments usually visible immediately or within hours (sometimes next business day). The page has no autopay setup/cancel or history FAQ, so those links stay null (use the biller's EZ-PAY portal). KUBRA Support Portal https://consumersupport.kubra.com/csp?id=kubra_csp_index (JavaScript app; loads 200 but content not readable by fetch). No consumer phone published.

entries.notes: Roster only; site returned a Cloudflare block so content was not read. entries.name: Meracord - debt settlement dedicated accounts
entries.notes: Formerly NoteWorld; long-time debt settlement dedicated-account processor (Tacoma, WA). meracord.com currently shows a 'Coming Soon' page, so no live help or login page was found. Contact your debt settlement company for the ledger and to stop drafts. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ , FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ , and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general . Background: in 2013 the CFPB sued Meracord (formerly NoteWorld) for processing illegal upfront debt-settlement fees (consent order, $1.376M penalty) - https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/201310_CFPB_meracord-complaint.pdf .

entries.notes: MyMMI account (https://www.moneymanagement.org/login): after registering an active DMP (instructions page) you can 'monitor creditor payments, setup automated deposits, access your monthly statements'. One-time deposit: MyMMI > DMP Deposits > Make A Deposit (step-by-step on /instructions/payments). Automated ACH deposits (monthly, bi-monthly or weekly) set up under DMP Deposit > ACH Deposit Signup (/instructions). To change or stop the automated deposit or cancel the plan, use the 'Deposits' section online or call Support 888-845-5669 - MMI recommends calling for time-sensitive deposit changes. Documents: upload in MyMMI or fax 888-812-5358. Former ClearPoint (and CredAbility) clients are MMI clients. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/ . Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent. Reviewer 2026-10-02: existing-DMP contact page re-read: manage regular DMP deposits online in MyMMI or call Support 888-845-5669; general 866-889-9347; document fax 888-812-5358. Former CCCS of Maryland (cccsmd.org) and CCCS Atlanta/ClearPoint (cccsatl.org, clearpointccs.org) domains now redirect to moneymanagement.org.

entries.entity_type: private (money transmitter, walk-in and online bill pay)
entries.service_area_detail: Cash bill payment at MoneyGram agents (Walmart, CVS, etc.) and online; biller search by name / receive code
entries.payment_processor: MoneyGram (in-house; biller search by company name or receive code)
entries.notes: REVIEW 2026-09-29: the old /mgo/us/en/bill-payment URL still answers but renders empty (client-side); current consumer pages are /us/en/services/bill-pay and the Bill Pay FAQ (both fetched via curl this session). Bill-pay page: 13,000+ billers (examples named: Federal Bureau of Prisons, Bilt, Payless Power, Ally Auto, Toyota Financial, 21st Mortgage, Texas and California Child Support); pay online, in the MoneyGram app, or in person with cash or debit at an agent location; same-day or next-day posting for many billers. FAQ: find a biller by company name or receive code in the app or online; fees vary by biller, amount, and posting speed; online limit is $3,000 per 30 days; online payment status is shown in the MoneyGram profile, but payments made in store show only on the receipt reference number, so call the biller with that number to confirm it posted; wrong account number means contacting MoneyGram and the biller immediately. There is no autopay (one-time payments only). Phone numbers embedded in the MoneyGram help-center page: contact 1-800-666-3947, support 1-800-922-7146, fraud 1-800-926-9400 (secondary fraud line 1-800-955-7777). entries.phone_customer_service: 1-888-660-7427 (Client Success Team, current clients; Mon-Fri 9am-9pm, Sat 9am-6pm ET); fax 888-688-3291; new clients 800-300-9550
entries.mail_payment_address: National Debt Relief, P.O. Box 2011, New York, NY 10272 (mailing address); corporate 180 Maiden Lane, 28th Floor, New York, NY 10038
entries.payment_processor: third-party dedicated-account provider (FDIC-insured trust account in client's name; provider not named on public pages)
entries.senior_programs: Retiree debt relief articles (e.g. https://www.nationaldebtrelief.com/resources/retiree-debt-relief/pay-off-debt/); no fee waiver program.
entries.notes: 'My Account' portal (login.nationaldebtrelief.com) plus portal chat/Apple Messages for Business (Mon-Sat 8am-9pm ET). FAQ: savings held 'in an FDIC-insured trust account... opened in your name, and you'll have ultimate control over its funds'; fee charged to the Dedicated Account only after a settlement and at least one settlement payment; 'you can cancel anytime without any penalties or fees other than any fees earned associated with prior settled debts'. To change the monthly deposit or stop drafts, call the Client Success Team. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ . Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ , FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ , and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general . ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint . Reviewer 2026-10-02: contact page re-read: voice support Mon-Fri 9am-9pm, Sat 9am-6pm ET at 888-660-7427; portal chat and Apple Messages Mon-Sat 8am-9pm ET; success@nationaldebtrelief.com; My Account portal login.nationaldebtrelief.com.

entries.name: Turnbull Law Group
entries.service_area_detail: Attorney-model debt resolution (law firm).
entries.notes: Roster only. Client program dashboard at turnbull.programdashboard.com. Law-firm debt settlement programs can be complained about to the state bar as well as the CFPB/state AG. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt ; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/ .
